topics.name: Counting and Place Value
objectives: Count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, beginning with 0 or 1, or from any given number
Count, read and write numbers to 100 in numerals; count in multiples of twos, fives and tens
Given a number, identify one more and one less
Recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones)
Identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations, including the number line
Compare and order numbers from 0 up to 100; use <, > and = signs
Read and write numbers to at least 100 in numerals and in words

keyVocab.definition: A single number symbol (0–9)
The value of a digit based on its position in a number
Groups of ten units
Single items, not grouped
Comparison of two numbers
A sensible guess at an amount
To look at differences and similarities between numbers

masteryIndicators: I can say what each digit in a 2-digit number represents
I can partition a 2-digit number into tens and ones
I can order numbers up to 100 from smallest to largest
I can find 10 more or 10 less than any 2-digit number
topics.starter: Show a 2-digit number on the board — pupils write tens and ones on mini-whiteboards
topics.guidedPractice: Use base-10 blocks: teacher models partitioning 34 as 3 tens and 4 ones; pupils repeat with different numbers
topics.independentPractice: Developing: place value charts with digit cards. Expected: order 5 numbers on a number line. Mastery: explain the difference between 37 and 73; write own examples.
topics.masteryCheck: Write the value of the underlined digit: 4_5, 7_2, 3_8. Then place 47, 74, 44 in order.

topics.name: Addition and Subtraction within 20
objectives: Read, write and interpret mathematical statements involving addition (+), subtraction (−) and equals (=) signs
Represent and use number bonds and related subtraction facts within 20
Add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero
Solve one-step problems that involve addition and subtraction using concrete objects and pictorial representations, and missing number problems

keyVocab.definition: Combining two or more numbers to find the total
Taking one number away from another
Has the same value as
A pair of numbers that add together to make another number
The answer to an addition
The answer to a subtraction

masteryIndicators: I can recall all number bonds to 10 and 20
I can use a number line to add and subtract
I can write a number sentence for a word problem
I can use the inverse to check my answer
topics.starter: Number bond ping pong: teacher says a number, pupils call out its pair to make 10
topics.guidedPractice: Use a number line: teacher models counting on to add, counting back to subtract; pupils try with different numbers
topics.independentPractice: Developing: number bond to 10 matching cards. Expected: solve 5 addition and 5 subtraction calculations. Mastery: write own story problems for given calculations.

topics.name: Addition and Subtraction within 100
objectives: Solve problems with addition and subtraction using concrete objects and pictorial representations
Recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently, and derive and use related facts up to 100
Add and subtract numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mentally
Show that addition of two numbers can be done in any order (commutative) and subtraction of one number from another cannot
Recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction

keyVocab.definition: Can be done in any order and give the same result
The opposite operation
Splitting a number into parts
Adding or subtracting through a multiple of 10

masteryIndicators: I can add two 2-digit numbers mentally
I can explain why addition is commutative
I can use inverse operations to check my calculations
I can solve two-step word problems
topics.guidedPractice: Column addition with place value columns: teacher models 45 + 37, linking to partitioning
topics.independentPractice: Developing: two 2-digit numbers < 50 (no regrouping). Expected: standard column addition and subtraction. Mastery: write a two-step word problem and solve it.
topics.masteryCheck: Work out 56 + 27 = ? and 83 − 46 = ? Show your method.

topics.name: Multiplication and Division
objectives: Solve one-step problems involving multiplication and division, using concrete objects, pictorial representations and arrays
Count in multiples of 2, 5 and 10
Calculate mathematical statements for multiplication (×) and division (÷) and write them using the multiplication (×), division (÷) and equals (=) signs
Show that multiplication of two numbers can be done in any order (commutative) and division of one number by another cannot
Solve problems involving multiplication and division, using materials, arrays, repeated addition, mental methods

keyVocab.definition: Repeated addition of the same number
Splitting into equal groups
Objects arranged in rows and columns
Groups that contain the same number of items
A number in a times table

masteryIndicators: I can count in 2s, 5s and 10s
I can use arrays to represent multiplication
I know the 2, 5 and 10 times tables
I can write multiplication and division fact families
topics.starter: Chant the 2 times table together, then jumble order on the board
topics.guidedPractice: Draw arrays: 3 rows of 4 — write the multiplication and division sentences
topics.independentPractice: Developing: complete array pictures to write × sentences. Expected: 2, 5, 10 times tables problems. Mastery: fact families — write all 4 related facts.
topics.masteryCheck: Draw an array for 4 × 3, write all 4 facts. What is 20 ÷ 5?

topics.name: Fractions
objectives: Recognise, find and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape or quantity
Recognise, find and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape or quantity
Recognise, find, name and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity
Write simple fractions e.g. 1/2 of 6 = 3 and recognise the equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2

keyVocab.definition: An equal part of a whole
The top number — how many parts we have
The bottom number — how many equal parts in total
One of two equal parts
One of four equal parts
Equal in value

masteryIndicators: I can find 1/2 and 1/4 of shapes and amounts
I can explain that fractions must be equal parts
I know that 2/4 = 1/2
I can find fractions of quantities (e.g. 1/4 of 12)
topics.starter: Show folded paper shapes — are these halves? Why or why not?
topics.guidedPractice: Fold and shade: fold a rectangle into halves, quarters; link to notation
topics.independentPractice: Developing: shade halves/quarters of shapes. Expected: find fractions of amounts. Mastery: explain equivalence with diagrams.
topics.masteryCheck: Shade 3/4 of a shape. What is 1/4 of 20? Explain how you know 2/4 = 1/2.

topics.name: Length and Height
objectives: Compare, describe and solve practical problems for lengths and heights
Measure and begin to record lengths and heights
Choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure length (m/cm/mm) using rulers

keyVocab.definition: How long something is
How tall something is
A unit of length; 100 cm = 1 m
A unit of length equal to 100 centimetres
A sensible guess before measuring

masteryIndicators: I can measure length in cm using a ruler correctly
I can compare lengths using < > =
I can estimate a length before measuring
I can order objects by length
topics.starter: Hold up classroom objects — pupils estimate length on mini-whiteboards
topics.guidedPractice: Model measuring a pencil with a ruler, starting from 0; common errors (not starting at 0)
topics.independentPractice: Developing: measure given lines. Expected: measure and compare 5 objects. Mastery: measure objects and order from shortest to longest with reasoning.
topics.masteryCheck: Measure these two lines. Which is longer? By how much?

topics.name: 2D and 3D Shapes
objectives: Recognise and name common 2D shapes: rectangles, squares, circles and triangles
Recognise and name common 3D shapes: cuboids, cubes, pyramids and spheres
Identify and describe the properties of 2D shapes, including the number of sides and line symmetry
Identify and describe the properties of 3D shapes, including the number of edges, vertices and faces
Compare and sort common 2D and 3D shapes and everyday objects

keyVocab.definition: A straight line that forms part of a 2D shape
A corner where two sides meet
A flat surface of a 3D shape
A line where two faces of a 3D shape meet
A shape is symmetrical if one half mirrors the other

masteryIndicators: I can name and describe 2D and 3D shapes using properties
I can sort shapes by their properties
I can find lines of symmetry in 2D shapes
I can explain why a shape belongs in a given category
topics.starter: Shape mystery bag: pupils feel a 3D shape and describe it
topics.guidedPractice: Teacher draws shapes on the board, class count sides, vertices together; record in table
topics.independentPractice: Developing: name shapes from pictures. Expected: complete properties table. Mastery: create a sorting rule for shapes and explain it.
topics.masteryCheck: Name this shape. How many sides, vertices, and lines of symmetry does it have?
